rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/station.py` and `reckon/crew/obligations.py` exist, `dispatch_review_for_run` resolves at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2656`, the quoted "inspect the follower's review pass" is at `reckon/crew/obligations.py:771`, and the "alive but slow … in the … stage" line is `slow_station_note` at `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:1146-1163`; the cited imas-efit-3c review run belongs to that host's crew home and is attributed as such, not to this repository.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the revised second case ("holds the station in its slow stage past the window with the reflex unable to run") is falsifiable, and the declared negative control (run the reflex only after the refresh stage completes) makes the first case dispatch late, so the head assertion fails at base.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-when puts every log under the run directory with its revision and literal command, and the timing arms run on the all_debug partition.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `tests/test_a_slow_refresh_does_not_hold_the_review_reflex.py` and the write paths name the mechanism, with no plan label, ticket number or version tag in code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence (§10 moved the review reflex into the station's tick, and the station snapshot already records `tick_stage`/`tick_age_seconds` for `per-project-refresh`), and the command the obligation must name exists as `reckon crew recover --dispatch-reviews`; the write-paths line is a scope declaration the earlier review declined and is left as-is.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — both clauses are one outcome, the review reflex no longer silently held by a slow station stage, closed by one verdict: timely dispatch, or an overdue obligation the coordinator can act on.
